entries.title: Psalms 75:1
segments:
, title). In impending danger, the Psalmist, anticipating relief in view of God's righteous government, takes courage and renders praise. 
 
    1. God's name or perfections are set forth by His wondrous works.

entries.title: Psalms 75:2
segments:
2, 3. These verses express the purpose of God to administer a just government, and in a time of anarchy that He sustains the nation. Some apply the words to the Psalmist. 
 
    receive the congregation--literally, "take a set time" (
), or an assembly at a set time--that is, for judging.

entries.title: Psalms 75:4
segments:
4-8. Here the writer speaks in view of God's declaration, warning the wicked. 
 
    Lift ... up the horn--to exalt power, here, of the wicked himself--that is, to be arrogant or self-elated.

entries.title: Psalms 75:6
segments: 6. promotion--literally, "a lifting up." God is the only right judge of merit.

entries.title: Psalms 75:8
segments: 8. in the hand ... a cup ... red--God's wrath often thus represented (compare

Jer 25:15). 
 
    but the dregs--literally, "surely the dregs, they shall drain it."

entries.title: Psalms 75:9
segments: 9, 10. Contrasted is the lot of the pious who will praise God, and, acting under His direction, will destroy the power of the wicked, and exalt that of the righteous.
